Q: ssh remote host identification has changed A:

It is showing due to the stored invalid ECDSA key. So we have to remove the ECDSA key from our master/controller machine by using the below command:

ssh-keygen -R 192.168.0.132

Here 192.168.0.132 is the remote system IP.

Q: Dynamic query is producing duplicate columns A:

Try

         CONCAT(' (CASE WHEN G.`', Year, '` = ''O'' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) ' )
         ORDER BY Year
         SEPARATOR ' + '
       )
    ,GROUP_CONCAT( distinct concat('G.`', Year, '`') order by year separator ',')
INTO @count_cols, @yearNames
FROM temp_years;

Q: how to get List of GID numbers and List of Sheet Names in Google Sheets? A:

we can do both tasks in multiple ways. here are some examples with requirements and limitations:

first step: share your spreadsheet (if you worry about privacy, just do not share the spreadsheet link with anyone)

LIST OF GID NUMBERS

for gids use:

=VSTACK(, IFERROR(LET(i, A1, INDEX(TOCOL(REGEXEXTRACT(SPLIT(DGET(
 VSTACK(i, IMPORTDATA("https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/"&i&
 "/preview?gid=0", "|")), i, VSTACK(i, "var gid")), "?gid=", ), 
 """(\d+)"""), 3)*1)), "Loading ..."))

  • recalculation every 60 minutes

  • shows only gids of unhidden sheets

  • sheets are in order of position

  • faster than 1h update needs manual user action via checkbox. recalculation time is fairly reasonable (0-1 min). now the mistery part: the output of IMPORTs is stored temporarily in some unknown shadow cache. this basicaly means that if you add/remove sheet, you may observe the old state for few more seconds, even after hitting that checkbox. however, the effect of the shadow cache can be prolonged even for few minutes, if you have 2 or more such formulae in your spreadsheet. here is the checkboxed fx version:

=VSTACK(, IFERROR(LET(x, A1, 
 y, "https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/"&x&"/preview?gid=0", 
 INDEX(TOCOL(REGEXEXTRACT(SPLIT(DGET(VSTACK(x, 
 IF(A2, IMPORTDATA(y, "|"), IMPORTXML(y, "//script"))), 
 x, VSTACK(x, "*var gid")), "?gid=", ), """(\d+)"""), 3)*1)), "Loading ..."))

and from here you can easily make a jumping links like:

=INDEX(IF(A5:A="",, HYPERLINK("#gid="&A5:A&"&range=C5", "jump to C5")))

these formulae can be modded to extract sheet names instead of gids, but you would get those sheet names with JS-style hex escape sequence in it if you would use exotic sheet names. to fix them you would need to run CHAR(HEX2DEC( functions:

LIST OF SHEET NAMES

for sheets try:

=VSTACK(, IF(A2, INDEX(LET(i, A1, x, CHAR(65535),
 y, IMPORTHTML("https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/"&i&"/view?gid=0", "table", 2), 
 z, IFERROR(INDEX(y, 2, 3), "LOADING ..."), 
 TOCOL(SUBSTITUTE(SPLIT(REGEXREPLACE(z, "(\n)'","$1"&x), CHAR(10)), x, CHAR(39)), 2)))))

  • recalculation every 60 minutes

  • shows sheet names of all sheets

  • show sheet names of hidden sheets

  • sheet names without JS-style hex escape sequence

  • sheets are in order of position

  • works with exotic sheet names

  • supports 99.99% of printable unicode characters

  • faster than 1h update needs manual user action via checkbox. recalculation time is fairly reasonable (0-2 min). also the mistery part: the output of IMPORT is stored temporarily in some unknown shadow cache. this basicaly means that if you add/remove/rename sheet, you may observe the old state for few more seconds, even after switching that checkbox. however, the effect of the shadow cache can be prolonged even for few minutes, if you have 2 or more such formulae in your spreadsheet. if it gets stuborn smash that checkbox few more times.

and again, active references easily done with BYROW like:

=BYROW(A5:A, LAMBDA(x, IF(x="",,IFERROR(INDIRECT(x&"!D1")))))
